listing.title: Colosseum Crypto World's Fair Hackathon | Superteam Argentina Track
listing.description:
One month. Build something that can win globally.

Start with an idea or bring an eligible early-stage project. Over one month, turn it into a working product that people can use, test and judge.

The Superteam Argentina track is for builders creating products on Solana with the ambition to compete globally. Build from anywhere in Argentina, connect with other founders and get support to turn your progress into a strong Crypto World’s Fair submission.

Ideas can enter. Working products win.

What should you build?

Build a product that solves a real problem and uses Solana as a meaningful part of the solution.

Consumer applications, payments, financial infrastructure, developer tools, gaming, DePIN, AI-powered products and other use cases are welcome. There is no required industry or business model: explain who your product serves, why it matters and how Solana makes it possible or meaningfully better.

Your final submission should include a functional product or prototype that demonstrates the core user experience—not just a concept, landing page or pitch deck.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for clear problems, thoughtful solutions and teams that make meaningful progress throughout the competition.

Build, speak with potential users, test your assumptions and improve the product. Bring evidence appropriate to your stage: user feedback, active testers, pilots, customer commitments, usage or revenue.

We value commitment, technical and product judgment, persistence and ownership. Use the mentors and resources available, ask for help when needed and turn feedback into action.

Show us what you built, what you learned and why you will keep building.

Support along the way

Superteam Argentina will support participating builders through product and technical office hours, group workshops, resources and feedback on product positioning, demos and pitches.

Selected projects may also receive relevant ecosystem introductions and visibility through Superteam Argentina’s channels.

The top ten shortlisted teams will be offered an intensive mentorship week, subject to mentor availability, to strengthen their products and prepare for their final presentations.

Workshop schedules, office hours and any confirmed Build Station activities will be shared through our community channels and events calendar. Participation in the program does not guarantee a prize, investment, partnership or admission to another program.

Who can participate?

The track is open to solo founders residing in Argentina and teams with at least one cofounder residing in Argentina. You do not need to be based in Buenos Aires.

To be eligible:

  • Build on Solana. Your submission must include a meaningful, functional Solana integration. Multichain products are welcome when Solana is part of the working product.

  • Meet the official hackathon requirements. Projects must comply with the applicable Crypto World’s Fair rules, including registration, prior work, funding and submission requirements.

  • Submit on both platforms. Submit your project to Crypto World’s Fair on Colosseum and to this Argentina track on Superteam Earn, meeting each platform’s requirements and deadline.

  • Disclose your starting point. Existing projects must clearly identify prior development, users, revenue and funding, and distinguish these from work completed during the competition.

Solo founders and multidisciplinary teams are equally welcome. You may join with an idea, but a working product is required for the final submission.

Submission requirements

When joining, provide a brief record of the project’s state at the official competition start: existing product and code, users, revenue, funding, team responsibilities and your first milestone. Keep a short weekly changelog so your progress can be reviewed.

Your final submission must include:

  1. Working product and demo video. A deployed link or accessible test environment, instructions for trying the product and a short video demonstrating its core functionality.

  2. Repository and technical overview. A repository link or private review access, plus a brief explanation of the architecture, Solana integration, key dependencies and relevant security considerations.

  3. Problem, users and validation. Explain the problem, target users and solution. Include verifiable evidence of user feedback, testing, usage, pilots, customer commitments, revenue or other relevant validation.

  4. Progress and disclosures. Include your starting-point record and weekly changelog. Clearly identify work completed during the competition, prior code or assets, third-party and open-source components, and material use of AI.

  5. Team and roadmap. Introduce the team, explain each member’s contribution and outline practical next steps beyond the hackathon.

Shortlisted teams must also submit a pitch deck and present at Demo Day. Presentation details will be shared with selected teams.

Participation notes

Submissions must accurately represent the product, its development history and its results. Fabricated users, metrics, revenue, partnerships or transactions may result in disqualification. Supporting evidence, including repository access, analytics or transaction records, may be requested.

AI-assisted development is welcome. Teams must disclose material use, explain their own contribution and understand the product they submit.

Smart-contract and financial products must clearly state their audit status, testing environment and known material risks. Demos must not expose users or funds to undisclosed risks.

Teams retain ownership of their projects. Submission grants Superteam Argentina a non-exclusive permission to showcase submitted public-facing materials for program promotion, without transferring project ownership or authorizing publication of private code.

Participation is subject to this listing, the applicable Superteam Earn Terms and Privacy Policy, and the official Crypto World’s Fair rules.

Join the community

Find upcoming workshops and events, connect with other builders and follow program announcements:

Prize pool — 10,000 USDC

1st Place 3,000 USDC

2nd Place 2,000 USDC

3rd Place 1,500 USDC

4rd Place 1,000 USDC

5th Place 500 USDC

University Award. 500 USDC

Best Demo Day Pitch. 500 USDC

Best User Experience . 500 USDC

Most Traction. 500 USDC

Total. 10,000 USDC

University Award — 500 USDC

Recognizes an outstanding project with meaningful student participation. At least one active team member must be enrolled at a university in Argentina at the start of the competition and demonstrate a substantive contribution to the project. Student status and contributions may be verified.

Best Demo Day Pitch — 500 USDC

Recognizes the strongest Demo Day presentation, considering clarity, narrative, delivery, product demonstration and the team’s ability to answer questions. A functional product is required; a slide-only presentation cannot win this award.

Most Traction — 500 USDC

Recognizes the strongest verifiable traction gained during the competition, assessed relative to the project’s stage and product type. Evidence may include active or repeat usage, paying customers, revenue, pilots, documented customer commitments or active testers providing substantive feedback.

Teams must distinguish existing traction from progress achieved during the competition. Social engagement, impressions and follower counts alone do not qualify.

Best Product Experience — 500 USDC

Awarded to the project that turns a strong idea into the clearest, most intuitive product experience. We’ll look at usability, onboarding, design consistency and attention to detail—not just a polished landing page.

Special awards are cumulative: a project may win one main placement prize and one or more special awards, provided it meets the requirements for each.


These prizes are awarded by Superteam Argentina. Eligibility for Colosseum prizes or other sidetrack awards is determined separately under their respective rules.
